subject: Edge adapter vs customer termination — ownership, DNS split, and cert rotation
messages:
From: Kevin Owen <kevin.owen@finbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, security@finbank.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TLS termination model for private VPC deployment

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we scope the Private deployment (VPC) for FinBank, our security team needs a clear recommendation on where HTTPS/TLS termination should happen for the Redwood endpoints that will live inside our VPC. Key constraints:

- We must use private FQDNs (no public certificates issued to external registrars for these names).
- All private keys used for TLS must be controlled by FinBank KMS/HSM unless we can justify otherwise to our auditors.
- Cert rotation proof and an auditable flow are required.

Can you outline the pros/cons of Redwood terminating TLS inside our VPC (edge adapter owned by Redwood) vs us terminating at our edge and using a passthrough to Redwood? Also any details on split-DNS, ACME allowances, and mutual TLS options would be helpful.

Appreciate a short doc we can include in the compliance package.

Thanks,
Kevin Owen
VP, Cloud Security
FinBank Inc.

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kevin Owen <kevin.owen@finbank.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TLS termination model for private VPC deployment

Hi Kevin — thanks for the clear constraints. I put together a concise ownership matrix and recommended options, attached. High level:

Option A — Customer-managed termination (recommended for strict compliance)
- You terminate TLS at your edge (your LB/proxy) and forward traffic to Redwood over a mutually agreed internal channel.
- DNS: customer-owned private zone pointing app.example.internal -> your LB; you create CNAME/A records that map to your internal gateway.
- Certs: customer generates and stores certs in your KMS/HSM; you can present certs to clients, and Redwood accepts connections from your trusted egress IPs or mTLS client certs.
- Pros: full key control, easiest for auditors.
- Cons: you manage rotation; requires stable internal routing and occasional config sync.

Option B — Redwood edge adapter termination (Redwood-hosted in your VPC)
- Redwood runs an adapter inside your VPC (dedicated or shared) that terminates TLS and speaks to the Redwood runtime over an internal network path.
- DNS: you delegate an internal subdomain or create split-DNS that points to the adapter.
- Certs: two sub-variants:
  B1: Customer provides certs (preferred in highly regulated setups). We accept a PEM bundle and will install on the adapter; rotation via automated CSR workflow or manual import.
  B2: Customer allows Redwood-managed short-lived certs (ACME/automated) inside your private zone via an ACME-sidecar the customer runs.
- Pros: simpler for client engineers, centralized observability and SLO enforcement.
- Cons: customers need to be comfortable with cert-handoff or run an ACME-sidecar; auditors will ask for the rotation proof.

Option C — Passthrough/TLS-aware proxy (terminate downstream)
- You terminate TLS at your edge and forward encrypted traffic to Redwood; Redwood does not see plaintext.
- Requires TCP-level forwarding to Redwood ports and coordination on SNI/ALPN.
- Pros: maximum key isolation.
- Cons: element of observability reduced; some features (e.g., request-level telemetry, streaming) need extra hops or instrumentation.

Attached: redwood_tls_ownership_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix with recommended choices by compliance level), edge-adapter-config-snippets.txt (example envoy/nginx blocks), csr-rotation-runbook.pdf (how we evidence rotation).

Connor and Karthik, can you add notes about mTLS and the runbook for rotation options? Kevin, if you can confirm which option (A/B/C) FinBank prefers, we can schedule a short workshop and propose a POC window.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: TLS termination model for private VPC deployment

Kevin / team — adding the infra perspective. Quick technical notes (keeps to the constraints Marissa laid out):

- SNI and split-DNS: for an adapter model we rely on customer-controlled private DNS to point the service hostname at the adapter IP. We recommend a delegated internal subdomain (e.g., rlw-adapter.finbank.internal) to avoid accidental public leakage.

- Key ownership options:
  1) Customer-supplied cert (PEM + chain): We accept the bundle and mount it readonly on the adapter. Rotation flow: customer initiates CSR rotation -> issues new cert via their CA -> supplies cert to Redwood via a secure transmission channel (S3 presigned + encryption or direct API upload) -> adapter hot-reloads. We provide CSR tooling if you need it.
  2) ACME-sidecar run by customer: sidecar performs ACME challenges against private DNS and writes certs to a shared volume that the adapter reads. This keeps private keys entirely on customer's VMs if the sidecar runs under your tenancy.
  3) Mutually authenticated TLS (mTLS): If you require mTLS for inbound (client->adapter), we support validating client certs issued by your CA; adapter acts as server TLS and verifies client cert presented by your edge.

- Rotation evidence for auditors: we recommend short-lived certs + automated rotation with an event log. Redwood can ingest rotation events (timestamp, fingerprint, uploader) and retain in audit logs for the agreed retention window. We can export a signed timeline for attestations.

- Performance & SLO: terminating at the adapter adds an extra hop but keeps latency negligible if adapter lives in the same AZ. For high-throughput customers we recommend dedicated adapter instances with ephemeral cert updates to avoid restarts.

- Config snippet example (Envoy TLS context) included in the attachment. Notes: prefer hot-reload and not full process restart to avoid KV cache resets.

Happy to run a short tech workshop to test the CSR flow with your PKI team.

-Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
